guarantees.claim: ctr_slice_idx is driven to the bitwise OR of all mr_ctr_slice_idx[0..Sp2VWidth-1] rails.
ctr_o_slice is driven to the bitwise OR of all mr_ctr_o_slice[0..Sp2VWidth-1] rails.
mr_err is asserted (1'b1) if any rail's value differs from the OR-combined output; otherwise it remains deasserted (1'b0).
guarantees.cond: mismatch between (ctr_slice_idx, ctr_o_slice) and any (mr_ctr_slice_idx[k], mr_ctr_o_slice[k])

assumptions.claim: Sp2VWidth is a positive integer matching the actual dimensions of mr_ctr_slice_idx and mr_ctr_o_slice arrays.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-range array indexing or silent misinterpretation of rail data.

assumptions.claim: The input rails mr_ctr_slice_idx and mr_ctr_o_slice are encoded using a scheme where all rails hold the same value (e.g., sparse/one-hot encoding), making bitwise OR the correct aggregation method.
assumptions.risk: If the actual masking scheme uses XOR shares or other non-identical encoding, the aggregated output will be incorrect, potentially bypassing the error detection or leaking secrets.

uncertain_points.claim: Bitwise OR is used to combine the multi-rail signals. It is unclear whether this is correct for the intended sparse encoding or if it could leak information or weaken error detection when rails are not one-hot.
uncertain_points.risk: If the actual encoding is not one-hot, the OR aggregation could produce unintended values, and the error detection may not cover all attack scenarios.

uncertain_points.claim: If Sp2VWidth = 0, the loops do not execute, ctr_slice_idx and ctr_o_slice remain 0, and mr_err stays 0. This may represent a valid but dangerous configuration that silently disables the aggregation and fault detection.
uncertain_points.risk: All error detection is bypassed; the design may assume at least one rail is present, leading to downstream use of a constant-zero value.
